answer: The prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening varies markedly across habitat types in a clear tripartite hierarchy: gardening-introduced plant prevalence is highest in anthropogenically modified, coastal, and hydrologically connected habitats (Coastal, Wetlands, Urban, and Riparian habitats; mean 0.57–0.79 species per plot; 36.1%–50.0% plot incidence); intermediate in agricultural systems (Croplands; mean 0.22 species per plot; 20.7% plot incidence); and lowest or virtually absent in undisturbed natural and semi-natural terrestrial habitats (Meadows, Coniferous forests, Broad-leaved forests, Scrublands, and Rock outcrops; mean 0.00–0.10 species per plot; 0.0%–7.7% plot incidence). Overall, over 91% of all gardening-introduced non-native plant records occur within coastal, wetland, urban, and riparian environments, reflecting the combined influences of high horticultural propagule pressure near human settlements and favorable moisture conditions in coastal and aquatic ecotones.

payload.workflow: Executed quantitative parsing and summary analysis on invaded_niche_pathways.csv (tab-delimited, N=632). Calculated plot-level counts, means, standard errors, invasion incidence rates (% plots invaded), and relative pathway shares across all 10 habitat classes. Tested omnibus differences using Kruskal-Wallis and ANOVA. Estimated Poisson Generalized Linear Models (unadjusted and controlled for landscape urban cover and road proximity) and binomial logistic models. Generated reproducible artifacts run_analysis.py and habitat_gardening_summary.csv.
payload.hypothesis: The prevalence of non-native plant species introduced via gardening differs significantly across habitat types, exhibiting the highest richness and incidence in coastal, wetland, urban, and riparian habitats (0.57–0.79 species/plot; 36.1%–50.0% of plots invaded), intermediate prevalence in croplands (0.22 species/plot; 20.7% invaded), and negligible prevalence in natural inland terrestrial habitats such as meadows, coniferous forests, broad-leaved forests, scrublands, and rock outcrops (≤0.10 species/plot; <8% invaded).
